chunks.text: RIVERPORT — Fire crews responded to a warehouse blaze on the east waterfront Tuesday evening. Officials confirmed 34 people were evacuated from nearby buildings as crews worked to contain the flames. No injuries were reported among residents or firefighters. The cause of the fire remains under investigation.

RIVERPORT — Fire crews responded to a warehouse blaze on the east waterfront Tuesday evening. Officials confirmed 19 people were evacuated from the surrounding block as smoke spread through the area. Firefighters battled the blaze for several hours before bringing it under control. Investigators have not yet determined a cause.

RIVERPORT — Fire crews responded to a warehouse blaze on the east waterfront Tuesday evening. Evacuations totaled 34 residents as the fire department cleared the immediate area for safety. Crews spent much of the night containing the blaze before declaring it under control. Fire investigators are examining the warehouse for the point of origin.

HARBOR DISTRICT — Voters narrowly decided the harbor district referendum on port expansion Tuesday. Officials estimated turnout at 52 percent of registered voters. The referendum passed by a margin of 6 percentage points, according to initial returns. Final certification is expected within two weeks.

HARBOR DISTRICT — Voters narrowly decided the harbor district referendum on port expansion Tuesday. Turnout was recorded at 47 percent of registered voters, election officials said. The referendum on port expansion passed by a narrow margin, according to unofficial results. City officials said the vote clears the way for planning to begin.

HARBOR DISTRICT — Voters narrowly decided the harbor district referendum on port expansion Tuesday. Election officials put turnout at 41 percent of registered voters. The margin of victory, initially reported at 6 percentage points, was revised to 9 points after final ballots were tallied overnight. The referendum authorizes the port authority to proceed with expansion planning.

NORTHGATE — Health officials confirmed a gastrointestinal illness outbreak at Northgate General Hospital this week. Hospital administrators said 34 cases have been confirmed hospital-wide since Monday. Officials have restricted visitor access to affected units as a precaution. The source of the illness has not yet been identified.

NORTHGATE — Health officials confirmed a gastrointestinal illness outbreak at Northgate General Hospital this week. The hospital reported 58 confirmed cases hospital-wide as of Thursday, according to administrators. Administrators have implemented enhanced sanitation protocols across all units. Health officials said the outbreak appears to stem from a common food source.

NORTHGATE — Health officials confirmed a gastrointestinal illness outbreak at Northgate General Hospital this week. Ward 3 alone has recorded 21 confirmed cases as of Thursday, according to hospital records. The hospital has expanded sanitation protocols across every unit in response to the outbreak. Administrators say the ward has been placed under additional monitoring.

NORTHGATE — Health officials confirmed a gastrointestinal illness outbreak at Northgate General Hospital this week. A hospital spokesperson said the hospital-wide count had reached 58 cases by Thursday. Staff have expanded cleaning procedures throughout the facility in response. Investigators are still working to trace the source of the illness.

SABLE CROSSING — Engineers closed the Sable Bridge indefinitely after inspectors found structural cracking Monday. Transportation officials said the bridge will remain closed until at least September 3 while repairs are completed. Traffic is being rerouted through Harrow Street in the meantime. Engineers are still assessing the extent of the structural damage.

SABLE CROSSING — Engineers closed the Sable Bridge indefinitely after inspectors found structural cracking Monday. City engineers said repairs are not expected to be finished before October 1. Commuters have been rerouted to Harrow Street. Officials have not ruled out a longer closure if further damage is found.

SABLE CROSSING — Engineers closed the Sable Bridge indefinitely after inspectors found structural cracking Monday. The department of transportation does not expect the span to reopen before September 3. Drivers are being directed to Harrow Street during the closure. A full structural assessment is underway.

MERIDIAN COUNTY — A civil jury delivered its verdict in the Meridian County negligence trial Thursday afternoon. Jurors awarded $2.4 million in total damages to the plaintiff. The panel ruled in the plaintiff's favor on six of the complaint's nine negligence counts, none of them naming the site supervisor. The two-week trial centered on a workplace injury claim.

MERIDIAN COUNTY — A civil jury delivered its verdict in the Meridian County negligence trial Thursday afternoon. The panel returned a total damages award of $3.1 million to the plaintiff. The trial, which spanned nearly two weeks, centered on a workplace injury claim. Plaintiff's attorneys called the verdict a significant win for their client.

MERIDIAN COUNTY — A civil jury delivered its verdict in the Meridian County negligence trial Thursday afternoon. Jurors awarded the plaintiff $2.4 million in total damages. On the counts specific to the site supervisor, the panel found for the plaintiff on two of three. The case stemmed from a workplace injury claim brought two years ago.

CAPE ARDEN — Tropical Storm Elva made landfall near Cape Arden early Wednesday, knocking out power along the coast. Utility officials said roughly 210,000 customers lost power as the storm came ashore. Downed trees and flooding blocked several coastal roads overnight. Crews were dispatched at first light to begin restoration work.

CAPE ARDEN — Tropical Storm Elva made landfall near Cape Arden early Wednesday, knocking out power along the coast. The National Weather Service clocked sustained winds at 90 mph at landfall. Power crews reported about 210,000 customers without electricity along the coastline. Emergency shelters opened in three coastal towns overnight.

CAPE ARDEN — Tropical Storm Elva made landfall near Cape Arden early Wednesday, knocking out power along the coast. Forecasters measured the storm's sustained winds at 90 mph as it came ashore. The regional utility reported 175,000 customers without power as of Wednesday morning. Officials said full restoration could take several days.

CAPE ARDEN — Tropical Storm Elva made landfall near Cape Arden early Wednesday, knocking out power along the coast. Sustained winds at landfall, initially reported at 90 mph, were revised to 105 mph after a full review of storm data Wednesday afternoon. The utility said 340,000 customers were without power. Officials said restoration crews from neighboring states have been called in to assist.

PORT OF DELACROIX — Dockworkers walked off the job at the Port of Delacroix Monday morning, halting cargo operations. Union officials said roughly 420 workers joined the walkout at the port. Cargo terminals reported a halt to all container handling for the day. Talks between the union and port management are expected to resume this week.

PORT OF DELACROIX — Dockworkers walked off the job at the Port of Delacroix Monday morning, halting cargo operations. The union local said about 650 workers walked off the job Monday. Shipping lines reported delays as container operations came to a standstill. Port management said it was assessing the scope of the disruption.

PORT OF DELACROIX — Dockworkers walked off the job at the Port of Delacroix Monday morning, halting cargo operations. About 420 dockworkers walked out at the port itself, union officials said. Organizers said the action is part of a coordinated national walkout involving roughly 3,200 dockworkers at ports across the country. The union has not said when normal operations might resume.

CROSSTOWN — Transit officials suspended Crosstown Line service after a signal failure near Union Yard Friday morning. Officials said the disruption delayed commuters by roughly 45 minutes during the morning rush. Shuttle buses were deployed to cover the affected stretch of track. Transit officials said normal service is expected to resume by 6 p.m.

CROSSTOWN — Transit officials suspended Crosstown Line service after a signal failure near Union Yard Friday morning. Riders reported delays of up to 70 minutes during the morning commute. The agency arranged bus shuttles to bridge the gap in service. The transit authority said it expects to restore normal service by 6 p.m.

CROSSTOWN — Transit officials suspended Crosstown Line service after a signal failure near Union Yard Friday morning. Crews worked through the morning to repair the signal equipment near Union Yard. The transit authority said riders should expect normal service to resume by 6 p.m. Shuttle buses were made available to affected commuters in the meantime.

OAKMONT — The Oakmont school district released its annual enrollment report Wednesday, showing a decline for the third year running. District-wide enrollment now stands at 14,200 students, according to the report. Officials cited declining birth rates and out-migration as the primary drivers. The school board is expected to discuss possible school consolidations at its next meeting.

OAKMONT — The Oakmont school district released its annual enrollment report Wednesday, showing a decline for the third year running. The district reported total enrollment of 14,200 students this year. At Oakmont High School alone, enrollment fell to 612 students, the steepest drop of any school in the district. Administrators said the high school's decline is driving talk of a possible boundary redraw.

OAKMONT — The Oakmont school district released its annual enrollment report Wednesday, showing a decline for the third year running. The report put district-wide enrollment at 13,800 students for the current year. Officials pointed to falling birth rates as the main factor behind the decline. The school board plans to review consolidation options at an upcoming meeting.

LAKESHORE — A toxic algae bloom spread across the northern basin of Lakeshore Reservoir this week, prompting a water advisory. Environmental officials estimated the bloom covered about 5.2 square kilometers of the northern basin. Health officials said the water advisory is expected to remain in effect for at least a week. Residents were advised to avoid contact with the affected shoreline.

LAKESHORE — A toxic algae bloom spread across the northern basin of Lakeshore Reservoir this week, prompting a water advisory. The reservoir authority initially estimated the bloom's extent at 8.5 square kilometers. Officials said the advisory would likely stay in place for at least a week while testing continues. Boaters and anglers were urged to steer clear of the northern basin.

LAKESHORE — A toxic algae bloom spread across the northern basin of Lakeshore Reservoir this week, prompting a water advisory. The bloom's extent, initially reported at 8.5 square kilometers, was revised to 12 square kilometers Thursday following an aerial survey. Reservoir officials said the water advisory remains in place indefinitely. Additional testing sites have been added around the northern basin.

REDMOOR — An independent audit of Redmoor's infrastructure bond fund uncovered a budget shortfall, officials said Tuesday. Auditors identified an $18 million shortfall in the bond fund's reserves. The city comptroller said the gap stems from cost overruns on multiple road projects. Officials pledged a full accounting at next month's council meeting.

REDMOOR — An independent audit of Redmoor's infrastructure bond fund uncovered a budget shortfall, officials said Tuesday. The audit found a $26 million gap in the bond fund. City officials attributed the shortfall to delays and rising construction costs. Council members called for an emergency budget session to address the gap.

REDMOOR — An independent audit of Redmoor's infrastructure bond fund uncovered a budget shortfall, officials said Tuesday. City auditors put the bond fund's reserve gap at $18 million. City officials pointed to cost overruns on several road projects as the cause. A full accounting is expected at next month's city council meeting.

MIDTOWN — City zoning officials issued a ruling on Midtown Stadium's seating capacity ahead of the fall season Thursday. The ruling sets the stadium's total capacity, including temporary standing-room sections, at 42,000 for the coming season. Officials said the figure reflects new safety guidelines adopted this year. Stadium management said ticket sales would proceed under the new limit.

MIDTOWN — City zoning officials issued a ruling on Midtown Stadium's seating capacity ahead of the fall season Thursday. The ruling caps the number of fixed seats within the stadium bowl at 36,500. City officials said the figure does not include standing-room areas. Stadium officials said the ruling would not affect planned renovations.

MIDTOWN — City zoning officials issued a ruling on Midtown Stadium's seating capacity ahead of the fall season Thursday. The city set the stadium's total capacity at 39,000 for the coming season. Officials said permanent seating is limited to 36,500 under the new rule. Stadium management said it would begin selling tickets under the new limits immediately.
